label: Aquinas, I q.12 a.1 co.: A thing is knowable in itself according to its actuality
interpretation: The opening reason for God's supreme intelligibility is actuality, explicitly distinguished from accessibility to a particular intellect. The second reply contrasts indefinite matter with unlimited form. The parallel at I q.14 a.3 co. applies the same principle to divine self-knowledge.
attribution: The passage states that each thing is knowable in itself according to the way in which it is in act, which is the premise.
